A service must implement a local interface.

What The Standard says

“stable contract” — The Standard minimizes the concrete public surface and presents stable contracts to consumers so implementations can change without coupling callers to internal business classes. read it here.
“Abstraction” — Foundation-service abstraction keeps upstream services independent of the technology and implementation behind a business operation. A local service interface is the contract that preserves that boundary. read it here.

Why it matters

A local interface defines the service boundary independently of its implementation. That abstraction supports controlled exposure, dependency injection, and isolated testing while preventing consumers from binding themselves to implementation details.

Bad code example

// Violates STX0013: A service must implement a local interface.
internal class StudentProcessingService { }

Good code example

// Follows STX0013
internal class StudentProcessingService : IStudentProcessingService { }
